field_evidence_needed: clear close photo of affected leaf
whether spots are on lower leaves or all leaves
weather_factors: high humidity and cloudy/rainy weather increase fungal leaf-spot pressure
water stress and nutrient imbalance can make brown spot worse
avoid any spray when rain or strong wind is expected
non_chemical_first: remove heavily infected leaves where practical and keep field sanitation
improve drainage and avoid standing stagnant water
use balanced nutrition; do not overuse nitrogen
check potash status and soil health before adding inputs
send clearer photos if symptoms are mixed or unclear
chemical_last_resort: only consider fungicide after field evidence and local threshold/risk assessment support disease diagnosis
follow label and local agriculture officer/KVK advice; do not rely on chatbot dosage
ask_expert_when: spots are spreading across the field
panicles or stems are affected
two different symptom types are present
the farmer already tried advice and crop worsened
common_issue_memory.safety_note: Prefer diagnosis plus non-chemical steps first. If chemical control is being considered, advise Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551 or local KVK/agriculture officer.

field_evidence_needed: photo of deadheart or white ear symptom
count of affected tillers per square meter or per hill
weather_factors: humid rice canopy and dense crop can favor pest survival
wind or rain can reduce spray effectiveness
stubble survival after harvest can increase next crop pressure
non_chemical_first: clip seedling tips before transplanting to reduce egg carryover
collect egg masses and conserve parasitoids
install pheromone traps and monitor weekly
destroy stubble after harvest and flood/till as community practice where feasible
conserve spiders and other natural enemies
chemical_last_resort: chemical control only after monitoring shows economic threshold is crossed
use locally approved product and label guidance through KVK/agriculture officer
ask_expert_when: deadheart or white ear is above threshold
damage is spreading despite IPM steps
the farmer cannot identify pest versus nutrient/stress symptom
common_issue_memory.safety_note: Do not recommend calendar-based pesticide use. Escalate threshold decisions to KVK/Kisan Call Centre when uncertain.

field_evidence_needed: photo of plant base near waterline
water level and recent nitrogen application
weather_factors: humid and dense canopy conditions can increase hopper pressure
excess nitrogen and continuous standing water can worsen outbreaks
rain/wind timing affects any intervention
non_chemical_first: drain excess water temporarily if field conditions permit
avoid extra nitrogen until pest pressure is clear
inspect plant bases and field patches, not only leaf tips
conserve predators and avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays
chemical_last_resort: only after hopper counts cross threshold and diagnosis is clear
follow label and local expert guidance; protect natural enemies
ask_expert_when: hopper burn patches are visible
more than one field patch is drying
prior pesticide use may have killed natural enemies
common_issue_memory.safety_note: BPH can worsen quickly; ask for field-base photos and advise KVK/Kisan Call Centre if patches are drying.

field_evidence_needed: stage: vegetative, booting, flowering, or grain filling
weather_factors: cloudy humid weather and leaf wetness increase blast risk
high nitrogen can increase susceptibility
neck blast near heading/grain filling needs urgent expert attention
non_chemical_first: avoid excess nitrogen and keep balanced nutrition
improve air movement where dense crop is causing prolonged wetness
remove volunteer/infected debris where practical
use resistant variety next season if blast is recurring
chemical_last_resort: fungicide decisions should be evidence-based and stage-aware
follow local recommendation and label; do not apply blindly
ask_expert_when: neck/panicle blast is suspected
large area is affected
symptoms spread after earlier advice
common_issue_memory.safety_note: For severe blast or neck blast, advise Kisan Call Centre 1800-180-1551 or KVK quickly.

field_evidence_needed: photo of yellow stripes/pustules on leaves
whether symptom is in patches or widespread
weather_factors: cool humid weather favors rust development
wind can spread spores between fields
avoid any spray if rain or strong wind is expected
non_chemical_first: confirm rust with clear leaf photos before treatment
avoid excess nitrogen
monitor field edges and patches every 2-3 days
use resistant varieties in future seasons
chemical_last_resort: chemical intervention should follow confirmed diagnosis and local advisory
follow label and KVK/agriculture officer guidance
ask_expert_when: yellow stripes are spreading
the crop is near booting/heading
multiple neighboring fields show similar symptoms
common_issue_memory.safety_note: Rust spreads fast. If diagnosis is likely, advise local KVK/Kisan Call Centre rather than guessing dosage.

field_evidence_needed: photo of aphids on leaf or earhead
rough count per tiller or earhead
presence of ladybird beetles or other natural enemies
weather_factors: mild dry spells can favor aphid buildup
rain may naturally reduce aphid pressure
spray timing should protect pollinators and natural enemies
non_chemical_first: check natural enemy population before action
avoid unnecessary broad-spectrum pesticide
monitor earheads and field edges
use water jet or localized non-chemical suppression where feasible on small patches
chemical_last_resort: only if counts cross local threshold and natural enemies are insufficient
follow label/KVK advice and avoid bee-active morning hours
ask_expert_when: aphids cover earheads in many patches
natural enemies are absent and crop is at grain filling
farmer is considering chemical spray
common_issue_memory.safety_note: Do not recommend calendar spray. Preserve natural enemies and escalate threshold decisions to local experts.

field_evidence_needed: photo of dried plants and root zone
weather_factors: dry soil and moisture stress increase termite damage risk
irrigation or rainfall can reduce stress-related termite injury
un-decomposed FYM can increase termite pressure
non_chemical_first: maintain appropriate soil moisture where irrigation is available
use well-decomposed FYM only
remove crop residues that harbor termites where feasible
confirm termite presence before treatment
chemical_last_resort: soil insecticide decisions need local diagnosis and label guidance
do not suggest treatment without root-zone evidence
ask_expert_when: large patches dry suddenly
root damage is visible
irrigation does not reduce symptoms
common_issue_memory.safety_note: Termite symptoms can resemble drought or root disease; ask for root-zone evidence before recommending treatment.

weather_factors: humid conditions around heading/flowering can increase disease risk
grain-quality disease decisions depend on stage and local advisory
non_chemical_first: do not use affected grain as seed
separate suspect grain from healthy produce
use certified seed and resistant varieties in future
confirm diagnosis through local expert before market/storage decision
chemical_last_resort: current-season chemical action is limited once grain symptoms are visible
future prevention should follow official seed treatment/local advisory
ask_expert_when: fishy smell or black grains are present
grain is intended for sale or seed
multiple spikes are affected
common_issue_memory.safety_note: Treat as an escalation/quality issue. Advise KVK/agriculture officer confirmation before sale, seed use, or storage decisions.
